title: 2004 AMC 10A Problem 23
statement: Circles \(A,\) \(B,\) and \(C\) are externally tangent to each other and internally tangent to circle \(D.\) Circles \(B\) and \(C\) are congruent. Circle \(A\) has radius \(1\) and passes through the center of \(D.\) What is the radius of circle \(B?\)

solutions.text:
Because circle \(A\) passes through \(D\)’s center and is internally tangent to \(D,\) circle \(D\) has radius \(2.\) Place \(D\)’s center at the origin and \(A\)’s center at \((-1, 0).\)

Let circle \(B\) have radius \(r\) and center \((x, r),\) using the symmetry of \(B\) and \(C\) about the horizontal axis. Tangency gives \[ \begin{aligned} (x + 1)^2 + r^2 &= (1 + r)^2, \\ x^2 + r^2 &= (2 - r)^2. \end{aligned} \]

Subtracting yields \(x = 3r - 2.\) Substituting into the second equation gives \(9r^2 - 8r = 0,\) so \(r = \dfrac{8}{9}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is D.
hints: Since \(A\) passes through \(D\)’s center and is internally tangent, circle \(D\) has radius \(2\)
Place the centers on coordinates; circle \(B\) of radius \(r\) has center at distance \(1 + r\) from \(A\) and \(2 - r\) from \(D\)
